Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Manage acute asthma exacerbation with bronchospasm likely precipitated by a recent URI; restart asthma controller therapy, provide short course oral steroids, and reinforce inhaler technique and use of a spacer; establish monitoring and escalation plan.
- 2) Address inhaler access/availability issue (patient ran out of Ventolin and Clenil Modulite ~1 week ago); ensure timely re-supply and counseling on adherence to relieve bronchospasm.
- 3) Work/readiness and return precautions: advise rest as needed, provide self-certification for 7 days, and outline red-flag symptoms warranting urgent medical review.
- 4) Documentation of patient education and follow-up: provide spacer with instructions; emphasize follow-up contact or visit if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within expected timeframe.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Chest tightness ongoing for about 3 hours.
- Onset, duration, progression: Onset ~3 hours ago; symptoms persisting; exertional dyspnea (shortness of breath with activity), worse with stairs; non-resting dyspnea.
- Associated symptoms: Wheeze, cough (non-productive), sore throat, runny nose; feeling under the weather; cough persists; slight nighttime cough.
- Past medical history: Asthma (since adolescence); prior asthma exacerbation requiring intubation during adolescence; hay fever/allergies; eczema in childhood; milk protein allergy in childhood.
- Medications: Inhalers used in the past—Ventolin (salbutamol) and Clenil Modulite; ran out about a week ago; not currently using inhalers.
- Allergies: None to drugs documented; dust/allergies noted.
- Social history: University student; not stated as smoker; no other social factors documented.
- Family history: Mother with eczema; father with asthma.
- Other: Patient expresses concern about needing intubation again; desires to obtain inhalers and relief of symptoms.

Objective:
- Not provided in transcript (no vitals or formal physical exam results documented).
- Reported findings: Able to walk stairs with mild exertional dyspnea; not short of breath at rest; no chest pain reported.
- No imaging or lab data available.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Issue: Acute asthma exacerbation with bronchospasm (likely) in context of recent upper respiratory infection and recent nonadherence to controller therapy.
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation. (Support from DDx: High likelihood for “Acute asthma exacerbation”; consistent with wheeze, chest tightness, SOB on exertion, recent URI, and history of asthma with past exacerbations.)
   - Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript): 
     - Viral-induced bronchospasm/acute bronchitis (Medium; link to recent URI).
     - Iatrogenic withdrawal/flare from stopping inhaled therapy (Medium; due to running out of meds ~1 week ago).
     - Pneumonia (Low; viral URI without fever or sputum and no focal exam documented).
     - Spontaneous pneumothorax (Low; no pleuritic pain or focal exam findings).
   - Investigations planned: None required emergently; no objective testing documented. Monitor symptoms; consider spirometry or peak flow if available and symptoms persist/worsen.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Restart inhaler therapy: Ventolin (salbutamol) and Clenil Modulite; dose/route/frequency not documented.
     - Short course of systemic corticosteroids: 5 days, two tablets in the morning.
     - Spacer device provided to improve inhaled drug delivery; instructions to use and prime.
     - Plan to continue controller therapy (Clenil Modulite) daily and PRN Ventolin; adjust if symptom control fails.
     - Safety: If Ventolin required more than every 3 hours at any time, seek medical attention.
     - Activity/work: Recommend rest while improving; self-certification for 7 days available.
   - Referrals: None indicated at this time.

2) Issue: Inhaled corticosteroid/reliever therapy interruption (nonadherence) contributing to symptom rebound.
   - Assessment: Inhaled controller therapy interruption likely contributed to current bronchospasm; consistent with DDx item “Iatrogenic/Intoxication: inhaled corticosteroid withdrawal or rebound bronchospasm due to stopping/losing access to daily controller therapy.”
   - Differential diagnoses (consistent): Acute asthma exacerbation; Viral-induced bronchospasm.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatments planned: Re-initiate Clenil Modulite and Ventolin; reinforce adherence; spacer use; return precautions.
   - Referrals: None.

3) Issue: Return-to-work and monitoring plan.
   - Assessment: Patient may require short-term rest and graded activity; self-certification for 7 days offered.
   - Plan: Advise rest until symptoms improve; provide guidance on warning signs for escalation (increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, lightheadedness) and to seek urgent care if these occur.

- Potential inconsistencies between transcript and DDx: No conflict noted (“conflict noted” not required as none identified).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor interruptions noted but overall coherent.

- Allergies: No known drug allergies documented.
- Current medications: Ventolin (salbutamol) and Clenil Modulite; ran out about a week ago; dose/route/frequency for restart not documented in transcript.
